# VirtualPLC

Local Mitsubishi MC protocol PLC simulator for client tests; Python 3.10+, stdlib only.
Install: pip install virtual-plc
Client: pip install pymcprotocol
  from pymcprotocol import Type3E
  c = Type3E(plctype="Q"); c.connect("127.0.0.1", 5000); c.close()
Start here: virtual-plc guide
Topics: run options client profiles ethernet embed faults memory troubleshoot divergences
Machine-readable: virtual-plc guide options --json; virtual-plc guide profiles --json; virtual-plc guide ethernet --json
Equivalent entry point: python -m virtual_plc guide

Rules:
- Use localhost; never connect to equipment or production networks.
- Client plctype and server profile must agree for iQ-R.
- CLI --ethernet-model infers its matching wire profile; explicit --profile conflicts are rejected.
- Ethernet guide JSON exposes separate runnable models and research-only FX5/RnCPU facts; no invented defaults.
- Optional --slmp-1e accepts batch 00..03 and diagnostics 15/16 only; type 15 returns bare F3, loopback 16 raw length+data, not a runnable FX5 model.
- CPU names have NUL fill by default; --text-pad 0x20 gives space fill.
- Seed direct Memory before start; snapshot after stop; use clients for live writes.
- Faults happen after execution; faulted writes are not rolled back.
- The client's single recv(4096) limits reads; keep batches under ~1000 words.
- PLC ordering, capacities and control policies remain partly unverified.
